name: Latrodectus hasselti
habitat: Dry, sheltered spots such as under pots, in letterboxes, sheds and outdoor furniture.
hazard_note: A redback bite can cause severe pain and needs medical care. Please do not handle it, and wear gloves when moving pots and garden things. If someone is bitten, use a cold pack and call 000 or the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26.
description: A small black spider; the female has a red stripe on her back. It builds a messy web in dry, sheltered places.

name: Atrax robustus
habitat: Burrows in moist, sheltered soil under rocks and logs and in garden beds, within about 100 km of Sydney.
hazard_note: A funnel-web bite can be life-threatening. Please do not touch it. If someone is bitten, apply a pressure immobilisation bandage, keep them still and call 000.
description: A large, glossy black spider that rears up when threatened. Males wander into gardens and houses on warm, humid nights in summer and autumn.

name: Trichonephila edulis
habitat: Large golden webs strung between shrubs and trees.
description: A large brown and grey spider with long legs whose big, strong web shines gold in sunlight. It rarely bites, and its bite is mild.

name: Argiope keyserlingi
habitat: Webs among shrubs, often with a bright white cross of silk.
description: A spider with silver, yellow and red bands that sits in the middle of its web with its legs held in an X.

name: Lampona cylindrata
habitat: Under bark and leaf litter, and indoors, where it hunts other spiders.
hazard_note: Its bite can be painful but is not dangerous. Please wash the bite and use a cold pack.
description: A slender, dark grey spider with a white tip on its abdomen.

name: Tiliqua scincoides
plant_note: Eats snails, slugs, insects and fallen fruit.
habitat: Dense low plants, rocks and logs to shelter under, and no snail bait.
description: A large, slow lizard with a broad head and a bright blue tongue it shows when threatened. It is harmless, and a friend to gardeners.

name: Intellagama lesueurii
habitat: Creeks, ponds and gardens near water, with rocks for basking.
description: A large dragon with a crest down its back and a long tail that suns itself near water and dives in when disturbed.

name: Pogona barbata
habitat: Open, sunny ground with logs and posts for basking.
description: A grey dragon with a spiny throat pouch that it puffs out and darkens when threatened.

name: Lampropholis delicata
habitat: Leaf litter, mulch and low plants with sunny gaps.
description: A tiny brown skink that darts through leaf litter catching small insects.

name: Pseudonaja textilis
habitat: Open country and suburbs, often near sheds, long grass and piles of timber or rubbish.
hazard_note: It is highly venomous. Please do not touch or try to move it. Please contact a licensed snake catcher or your council. If someone is bitten, apply a pressure immobilisation bandage, keep them still and call 000.
description: A slender, fast snake, plain brown in colour, that rears up in an S shape when threatened.

name: Pseudechis porphyriacus
plant_note: Hunts frogs, including cane toads, which can poison it.
hazard_note: It is venomous. Please do not touch or try to move it. Please contact a licensed snake catcher or your council. If someone is bitten, apply a pressure immobilisation bandage, keep them still and call 000.
description: A glossy black snake with a red or pink belly.

name: Morelia spilota
hazard_note: It is not venomous but can bite. Please leave it alone, or contact a licensed snake catcher to move it.
description: A large, patterned python that squeezes its prey and often lives in roof spaces.

name: Dendrelaphis punctulatus
habitat: Trees and shrubs, often near water.
description: A slender, harmless snake, often green or olive with a yellow belly, that moves quickly through trees.

name: Ranoidea caerulea
habitat: Water tanks, downpipes and leafy plants near water.
description: A large, plump green frog with a deep, croaking call, often found around houses.

name: Limnodynastes peronii
habitat: Ponds and still water with plants at the edges. Its call is a single 'tok'.
description: A brown frog with dark stripes down its back that lays its eggs in a floating foam nest.

name: Litoria fallax
description: A tiny green or brown tree frog with a white stripe along its side.

name: Litoria peronii
habitat: Trees and shrubs near ponds and dams. Its call sounds like a cackling laugh.
description: A grey-brown tree frog with green flecks, yellow and black marbling in its armpits, and a cross-shaped pupil.

name: Crinia signifera
habitat: Damp ground near ponds, drains and soaks, calling with a cricket-like chirp.
description: A tiny brown frog with very varied markings.

name: Rhinella marina
habitat: Lawns, gardens and anywhere near water and light.
hazard_note: Its skin glands carry a poison that can kill dogs and cats that mouth it. If a pet mouths a toad, please wipe its gums with a damp cloth and take it to a vet.

rules.text: Cane toads are not a prohibited or restricted animal in Queensland, but everyone must take reasonable steps to manage them on their land.

description: A large, warty, brown toad with a bony head and big poison glands behind its eyes, introduced in 1935. Native frogs are often mistaken for it, so please check before acting.
